bytes_per_token.note: bytes / tokens; the first two count the <|bos|> tokens, as the trainer's bits per byte does

unigram.note: entropy of the distribution of tokens in the training set, <|bos|> included

rank_frequency.note: counts[r-1] is the number of occurrences in the training set of the token of rank r, ids[r-1] its id

zipf_fit.note: least squares of log10(count) on log10(rank) over ranks 10..1000: count ~ rank^(-exponent)

train.note: tokens of text in a document, the <|bos|> token not counted

histogram.note: counts[i] documents have edges[i] <= length < edges[i+1]; the edges grow by a factor 2^(1/4)

val.note: tokens of text in a document, the <|bos|> token not counted

histogram.note: counts[i] documents have edges[i] <= length < edges[i+1]; the edges grow by a factor 2^(1/4)

token_length_bytes.note: by_type[k]: tokens of the vocabulary that are k bytes long; by_occurrence[k]: their share of the training text tokens

ngrams.smoothing: interpolated Kneser-Ney, one discount per level D = n1/(n1 + 2 n2), uniform distribution below the unigrams
ngrams.note: sample_bits_per_token is the entropy of the n-th token given the n-1 before it under the counts of the sample itself (no smoothing; it falls towards zero as n grows because most long n-grams occur once); held_out_* is the cross-entropy of the smoothed model on the held-out stream, <|bos|> tokens included

compressors.note: the held-out documents joined by line breaks, compressed as one stream: 8 * compressed bytes / val bytes

checks.note: every training shard read in full; a held-out document is 'found' if a training document has exactly its tokens; the last check encodes every held-out document with the pure-Python gptpp.bpe and compares with val.bin
